concept: Dropzone is a tray window cut into the body where a file can be let go, the way a device has a recess where a card or a tape drops in. The same window carries a real key that opens the file picker, so letting go is a shortcut and never the only way in.

default_to_avoid.pattern: dashed-border dropzone box with a cloud icon that turns blue and tinted when a file is dragged over it
default_to_avoid.why_not: A dashed outline is a generic web frame with no place in the body, and a blue tint tells drag-over by colour alone and spends a second accent.

default_to_avoid.pattern: dropzone that is a drag target only, with the picker hidden behind a click on the empty area
default_to_avoid.why_not: People who cannot drag, and everyone on a keyboard, have no visible part to reach; the picker needs a real key inside the window.

references.source: Braun ET 66 calculator (Dietrich Lubs, 1987): the entry window is a recess in the body
Braun T 1000 world receiver (Dieter Rams, 1963): a printed legend beside each window says what the part is for
system/FORM.md input class: recessed well, full width of its column, never a bordered rectangle floating on the page
WCAG 2.2 2.5.7 Dragging Movements: a single-pointer alternative to every drag

derivation.consequence: the window is recessed into the body (inverse light)
derivation.form: The tray takes surface.sunken and elevation.well like Input, so it reads as a place cut into the case that takes something in.

derivation.consequence: every part keeps ≥44px hit area even when it draws smaller
derivation.form: The Choose key inside the window is the 44px Button, and the window itself is three key-heights tall, so there is a large target for a pointer.

derivation.consequence: every mechanism has its keyboard map
derivation.form: A press, Enter or Space on the real key opens the picker, so the keyboard has the same way in as a drop.

derivation.consequence: fixed positions, so a unit's layout does not reflow between states
derivation.form: A file held over the window changes the words, the glyph and the weight of the rim, and nothing moves or resizes.

derivation.consequence: orange appears once per unit, on the primary control's body only
derivation.form: The Choose key is a plain key in body colour and the held-over rim is ink, so the window never takes the unit's one orange.

options.name: tray window with a heavier rim on drag-over
card slot that opens wider on drag-over
printed crop marks that close in on drag-over

variants.reason: A reuses the recessed window of Input and Display, so it reads as a place that takes something in, and its held-over state shows in three ways (rim, words, glyph) with no reflow. B changes height and so moves what stands below it (against P6), and C is flat printing with no recess, which looks like a viewfinder and not a tray.

root.why: The tray is a sunken window with the inverse light and a ring rim, three key-heights tall, so a dragged file has a wide place to land.

glyph.why: A dot-matrix mark sits above the words and changes shape when a file is held over, so the state does not rest on colour.

title.why: The title says what the window does now, in the emphasis size and medium weight, with a line box tall enough for Thai marks.

hint.why: The second line is secondary ink on the sunken plastic at more than 4.5:1 and tells the person the other way in.

key.why: The Choose key is a real 44px Button in the tab order, so opening the picker never depends on dragging or on a click in empty space.

data-over=true.why: While a file is held over, the rim goes heavier, the words change to Release to add and the glyph changes, all inside the same box so nothing reflows.

data-disabled=true.why: A disabled tray loses its recess shadow and fades to half, takes no drop, and its key is disabled too.

@media forced-colors: active.why: In forced colours the window keeps a real border and the held-over rim draws in the Highlight colour.

@media prefers-reduced-motion: reduce.why: Under Reduce motion the rim changes at once, with no fade.

outline-color.why: Only the rim changes when a file is held over, on motion.hover, because a state change is the only thing that may move; the words and glyph swap at once.
